# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - Expansion Pack

The flagship expansion pack for the port, and the worked example of the
[expansion-pack format](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack.md). Everything in
it is written with the files, rules and tooling any modder has - nothing in
the engine knows this pack by name - so anything Rebirth does, another pack
can do.

## The story

Long before the Mist, a sea tower stood on the cliffs past Rim Elm, looking
west over a scatter of islands. Its keepers, the **Genesis Wardens**, were
root-tenders before they were bell-keepers: the islanders' tale says the
tower stands on a root of the first Genesis Tree, and that its foundation
stone was cut from that root. Later the Wardens hung a great bronze bell
over the stone, to call the fishing boats home through the sea fog.

When the Mist came, its first breath came in off the sea and reached the
tower before anything else. The last Warden, **Ysolde**, could not stop
the Mist, but she could hold that first breath: she sealed it under the
foundation stone and bound herself into the stone to keep it there. That
is the **Warden's Stone**. The bell has not rung since, and Rim Elm half
forgot the tower behind the Mist.

Now the Genesis Trees are pushing the Mist back, and the last of it sinks
toward the oldest thing that still holds a piece of it: the tower. It
brings what it swallowed - a beacon's fire, an overgrown grove, the engine
that turned the bell, the prayers of drowned sailors - and each settles on
a floor and will not let go. At the top, the Mist's grip on the tower
takes a shape, the **Hollow Sovereign**. The party climbs to make it let
go, floor by floor. Ysolde asks one more thing after the throne: she can
release her seal only once someone strong enough stands ready to meet
what is under it. When that is done, the bell rings once.

Behind the tower's sea gate lie the **Lantern Isles**, which the Mist
covered longest. The islanders lived through it by keeping lanterns lit
along every path, where the **rootlight** grows: ordinary green shrubs
that drink from a root running close under the ground, and glow faintly
with it. The Mist never took ground over a living root. The root surfaces
in the **Singing Grotto**, where the Pearl once sang back to the tower's
bell across the water.

The pack tells that history in pieces the player can pass by: Ysolde's
journal pages on the floors, the Atrium's murals, Imre the scholar in
Tolva's Haven, the rootlight itself and the root in the grotto. It is fan
lore standing beside the retail story: the Genesis Trees push the Mist
back, as they do in the game, and nothing here says what the Mist is.

The retail game ends with nothing left worth fighting past level 60 or so.
Rebirth is built for the climb from there to 99.

## What's inside

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `pack.toml` | The manifest. |
| `maps/genesis_1f.toml` ... `_8f.toml` | The eight floors of the tower. |
| `battle.toml` | The derived monsters, formations (five in waves), the tower and Isles encounter tables, one retail-scene override, eight bosses (every one refuses Run). |
| `progression.toml` | The level curve past 40, EXP and gold multipliers, enemy scaling, level-up rewards at 55, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 99. |
| `quests.toml` | An eleven-quest main chain ending in the First Breath, ten side quests, four Isles quests, five challenges. |
| `dialog.toml` | Every line the pack says. |
| `cutscenes.toml` | The tower intro on the first arrival in the Atrium, the voice on the throne speaking at the Gambler's Rest, the Sovereign rising before the last fight and the throne breaking after it, and each floor keeper's intro and fall. |
| `modes.toml` | Two poker tables, two card duels, three golf courses, three race tracks (one each on the 1F floor), two prop-hunt arenas. |
| `cards.toml` | The trading cards, boosters, dealer and drop rules. |
| `items.toml` | 20 pack items (consumables, the Warden and Vigil gear, accessories), the Vigil set and the 5F Tower Armory. |
| `audio.toml` | The pack's own drone track, its ambient loops (fire, water, wind, crowd, engine, drips, surf, birdsong) and boss stings, the tower bosses' victory music, the mode music at the Rest's tables. |
| `assets/audio/` | WAV files synthesised by `scripts/models/generate_rebirth_audio.py`. |
| `assets/models/` | glTF models: the ember crystal (`scripts/models/generate_ember_crystal.py`) and the floors' set pieces - sundial, fountain, armillary ring, lanterns, cogs, banners, obelisks, braziers, and the Isles' lamp posts, produce crates, rowboats, driftwood, shells, ferns and marram grass (`scripts/models/generate_rebirth_props.py`). |
| `arts.toml` | One Tactical Art per hero learned on the climb (level 55, after the Cinder Warden) and one Knell finisher each (level 80, after the Iron Regent), chained from that art into a retail one; all on the heroes' own retail clips. |
| `spells.toml` | Four tower Seru - Hearthfire, Verdant Bloom, Grove Fang, Tempest Dive - each cast as the retail Seru it grew from and taught by capturing its pack monster once that floor's keeper falls. |

### The tower

| Floor | Map | Base scene | Party level | What's there |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1F Atrium | `genesis_1f` | `tower` (Sky Gardens Tower), built from scratch | 40-48 | The Warden's Stone, the training gauntlet bell, the card dealer, the stair down to Rim Elm |
| 2F Ember Stair | `genesis_2f` | `rugi` (Rogue's Tower), built from scratch (37 x 40) | 50-55 | Boss: the Cinder Warden; the forge and the ash shrine |
| 3F Hanging Garden | `genesis_3f` | `teien` (Sky Gardens), built from scratch (39 x 40) | 55-60 | The Garden Gauntlet (four waves), the Gilded Herd |
| 4F Verdant Vault | `genesis_4f` | `concnow` (Conkram), built from scratch (49 x 37) | 60-68 | Boss: the Verdant Colossus; the Root Archive and the Flooded Cloister |
| 5F Gambler's Rest | `genesis_5f` | `koin1` (Sol Tower rooms), built from scratch (37 x 30) | - | No monsters; Keeper Odalric and his five tables |
| 6F Engine Deep | `genesis_6f` | `chitei2` (Jette's Fortress), built from scratch (35 x 37) | 70-78 | Boss: the Iron Regent; the Engine Gauntlet (six refills) |
| 7F Sanctum of Echoes | `genesis_7f` | `korb3` (Sol Tower underground), built from scratch (33 x 34) | 80-88 | Boss: the Azure Seraph |
| 8F Hollow Throne | `genesis_8f` | `taiku2` (Zora's Floating Castle), built from scratch (31 x 36) | 88-99 | Superboss: the Hollow Sovereign, in two waves; the Herald Watch in the nave |

Every floor carries the detail layer
([`expansion-pack-maps.md`](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack-maps.md#decorations)).
The Atrium's walls stand (the tower's stone blocks and a low south parapet),
Rogue's Tower torches line them and light the hall under enhanced lighting,
vines, grass, rubble and Rim Elm's barrels and crates dress the floor (props
from three scenes, their textures copied into free VRAM), four ember
crystals - the pack's own glTF model, `assets/models/ember_crystal.glb` from
`scripts/models/generate_ember_crystal.py` - float, turn and glow round the
dais, a rune ring turns before the Warden's Stone, the dais flagstones
drift, and mist curls over the outer ring. Its pillars are decorations
wearing octagonal stone decals over the retail mesh's black caps, moss and
worn-stone decals break up its floor, embers rise from the crystals and
sparks hang round the Warden's Stone.

The floors above are laid out from scratch (`geometry = "none"`) out of
their base scenes' textures and meshes, each bigger than the retail room it
borrows and each a set of rooms on several floor tiers, laid for the follow
camera: a low parapet on every room's north (camera) edge, full walls on
its far and side edges.

- **2F Ember Stair** climbs away from the camera in four flights: the
  lower hall between two lava moats (the Rogue's Tower's water turned to
  fire and set flowing by `[[materials]]` tint and scroll), the forge and
  the ash shrine off it, the middle hall between lava runs and four ember
  pillars, the upper terrace with the Cinder Warden's brazier on its dais
  (the tower's flame ring turning, two pyre wisps, a rune circle).
- **3F Hanging Garden** steps up three terraces: the lower garden's
  parterre round a fountain, the orchard and the rose arbour's brick
  arches either side of the raised sundial plaza, the upper terrace's
  reflecting basin and the belvedere open to the sky.
- **4F Verdant Vault** is climbed down into: a high gallery rings the
  colonnade, steps drop into the sunken court where the moss over the
  Colossus breathes under the vault's heart; off the galleries, the Root
  Archive and the Flooded Cloister.
- **5F Gambler's Rest** is a hall with the keeper's long bar, the High
  Table and the hearth; the card room (the Warden's Duel table, the card
  dealer) and the games room (Tower Game Night, the arcade cabinets, its
  own music) off it; the lounge's piano stage and the stair up behind the
  bar. Old Mott, a Sol casino slot player whose motion stream seats him,
  waits on a bar stool.
- **6F-8F**: spark showers, steam and two flywheels in the Engine Deep;
  three orbiting echo crystals and blue motes in the Sanctum; dust, violet
  motes and a low haze in the Hollow Throne.

Each floor's stairs chain to the next (`exits` with `to = { kind = "map" }`);
the 1F stair down leads to Rim Elm. The 1F stair up is the seal Ysolde
lifts: it stays shut (`requires = { flags = ["tower_open"] }`, with a locked
line) until the Warden's Trial is done.

### The Lantern Isles

Past a sea gate in the Atrium's west wall (open once Ysolde has first
spoken, so a level-30 party grows here into the Warden's Trial) lies an
outdoor region of four maps, each laid out from scratch at
the field grid's larger sizes and dressed with the detail layer. The
four stand on a sculpted `[terrain]` (sloping shores, cliffs, dunes, a
hill, a forest of wooded banks, a rock floor and a pool under animated
water with rolling surf; `docs/formats/expansion-pack-maps.md`,
"Terrain"). The grotto's rock and the Thornwood's lane and turf are
borrowed from other retail scenes' VRAM (`from`), and each map has its own
ambience (`[audio]`: surf, wind, drips, birdsong, the village's murmur):

| Map | Base | Size | What is there |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isles_beach` Saltwind Beach | `town01` | 64 x 36 | The sea-stair landing, marram dunes and palms, the fishers' cove (two rowboats drawn up, a net rack), a weed-dark tideline with driftwood, shells and rock clusters, surf, a ruined jetty, the ferrywoman; shore encounters |
| `isles_village` Tolva's Haven | `town01` | 64 x 50 | Huts, the well and windmill, the lodge (`rest`), Pell's Trading Post (`shop` `isles_trader`), villagers; the Village Duel table under the great tree and the Mist Lantern Table below the lodge (`modes.toml`); a dusk mood |
| `isles_thornwood` The Thornwood | `vell` | 112 x 56 | A lane winding through clumped old forest: Mushroom Hollow, a ford, the old shrine and its lookout, the hermit's camp round his log (Hermit Ost, Rim Elm's old man borrowed into the forest), a fern dell, and the ruined court with the Thornwood Queen (`isles_hive_queen`) inside the gate |
| `isles_grotto` The Singing Grotto | `cave01` | 72 x 60 | Four chambers under the ruins linked by passages: the antechamber, the crystal gallery, the mushroom grotto round its spring, and the singing pool with the Pearl on its islet; a floor of moss, scree and seep stains, with rock shelves and standing pools |

The region's monsters, formations, encounter tables and mini-boss are
`isles_*` entries in `battle.toml`; its four quests (`isles_landfall`,
`isles_nets`, `isles_thornwood`, `isles_pearl`) and their lines are in
`quests.toml` and `dialog.toml`.

### Bosses

| Boss | Floor | Built on | Music | Formation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cinder Warden | 2F | Caruban (Lv3) | 28 "Attack!" | the Warden and two Pyre Wisps |
| Verdant Colossus | 4F | Berserker (Lv3) | 32 "Apostles of the Mist" | the Colossus and a Moss Grude |
| Iron Regent | 6F | Jette | 31 "Cort's War" | the Regent and two Brass Sentinels |
| Azure Seraph | 7F | Lapis | 29 "The Cold Koru" | the Seraph alone |
| Hollow Sovereign | 8F | Dohati, then Songi | 61 "Apocalypse" | wave 1: the Sovereign and two Throne Heralds; wave 2: the Sovereign Unbound |
| Echo of the Throne | 8F | Songi | 73 (Wild Arms battle) | repeatable rematch: the Unbound and a herald, two more heralds refilling |
| The First Breath | 1F, past 99 | Rogue | 61 "Apocalypse" | the Breath alone, calling two heralds at 70% and two more at 40% |
| Thornwood Queen | the Isles | Queen Bee | 28 "Attack!" | the Queen and two Ruin Wasps |

All but the Echo are `once = true`: their gold and item rewards pay out on
the first victory and the boss refuses a second start. The Echo is the
repeatable endgame fight. Every boss is `no_escape = true`, which also seats
it on the battle loader's scripted profile (ATK x5/4, both defences x2).

Each keeper's fight opens on its intro cutscene (`battle.toml` `intro`):
the shot finds the keeper's place, the entrance sting hits, the screen
flashes the keeper's colour and its title banner rises. Each phase change
rings the phase shimmer under the script's banner line, and a won fight
closes back on the floor (`outro`) on the falling knell and a banner of
what is left.
Each tower boss fights on a retail stage of its own picking (`battle.toml`
`stage`), not the stage under its floor's room: the Warden on Bio Castle's
lava floor (`jouinc`), the Colossus in Mt. Letona's wood (`retona`), the
Regent in Sol Tower's machine hall (`korb3`, its second stage), the Seraph
under the moonlit pillars of Noa's Conkram dream (`urudre2`), the Sovereign
under the Mist's violet sky (`jou`), the Echo in Dohati's hall (`dohaty`)
drained violet by a stage `tint`, and the First Breath on Uru Mais's
storm-swept peak (`uru`). The night and Mist stages carry a lifting `tint`
so the phase shades still read.

Every boss fights with a boss script (`[monsters.<key>.script]` in
`battle.toml`) instead of its base monster's retail AI. Each move is the base
monster's own swing or a spell-table id, so damage and animation are the
disc's:

| Boss | Script |
|---|---|
| Cinder Warden | Below half its armour splits: attack x1.3, speed x1.25, Lava Breath and a double swing at the weakest member. Enrages at round 15. |
| Verdant Colossus | Below 60% it heals 15%, hardens, calls a Moss Grude back and telegraphs Earthquake; below 25% it turns to earth and rages. |
| Iron Regent | Strikes whoever hits hardest; at two thirds and one third it summons a Brass Sentinel into an empty seat, and its last phase telegraphs Hyper Crush. |
| Azure Seraph | Below half turns to thunder, calls two Fallen Lanterns (the drowned choir) and telegraphs Water Hazard; from round 14 the sky opens: Thunder Storm and triple swings. |
| Hollow Sovereign | Three phases: at two thirds it calls a herald, at one third it is unmade and telegraphs Grand Beam. A last stand, and an enrage at round 20. |
| Sovereign Unbound | Chaos Flare from the start; below half a telegraphed Thunder Burst. A last stand of its own. |
| The First Breath | Fire, then wind (70%: double swings at the weakest, Chaos Flare, two heralds), then thunder (40%: heals 10%, two more heralds, a telegraphed Grand Beam with the chime). A last stand, and an enrage at round 22. |

Their banner lines are the `warden_*`, `colossus_*`, `regent_*`, `seraph_*`,
`sovereign_*`, `unbound_*` and `breath_*` lines in `dialog.toml`.
Every telegraphed spell is `ignore_mp`: once a boss has charged it, it lands
whatever MP the boss has left.

### Quests

The main chain climbs the tower: **A Tower Wakes** (starts on its own at
level 30) -> **The Warden's Trial** -> **The Ember Stair** -> **The Hanging
Garden** -> **The Verdant Vault** -> **The Gambler's Rest** -> **The Engine
Deep** -> **The Sanctum of Echoes** -> **The Hollow Throne** -> **The Last Vigil**
(reach level 99 and return to the stone) -> **The First Breath** (what
Ysolde's seal held under the stone all along). Each boss quest has a minimum
level (50, 60, 70, 80, 88), so the chain paces the climb, and every keeper's
payoff line - and each floor's arrival line - names the level the next one
asks for, so the player always knows where to go and when.

The Isles quests open as soon as Ysolde has spoken (**Landfall**, **Torn
Nets**, **The Thornwood Queen**, **The Pearl Below**): the region is the
bridge from the tower's opening at 30 to the trial at 40. The elder's
welcome that closes Landfall also sends the party into the Thornwood, one
talk and one box, its Queen tuned for 35. A
few NPCs answer progress through `line_after`: the Warden's familiar once the
throne is empty, the 5F card room once the engine stops and the throne
falls.

Side quests: **Every Floor** (stand on all eight floors), two repeatable
bounties (**Ironhide Ogres**, **Brass Sentinels**), **A Remedy for Stone**
(hand in five Healing Fruit), **The Gilded Herd**, **Seasoned Hunter** (a
hundred wins), **Echo of the Throne** (repeatable superboss rematch),
**The Keeper's Tables** (win each of the Rest's five tables), **High
Roller** and **Trial Master** (clear three challenges).

Challenges: **Bare Hands** (ten rounds, no items, no magic), **Garden
Sprint** (the Garden Gauntlet in twelve rounds), **Lone Fist** (Vahn alone
against the Engine Gauntlet), **Humble Before the Seraph** (nobody above level
85), **Echo Storm** (the Echo at x1.5 strength within fifteen rounds).
Bare Hands is armed at the 1F trial stone (`kind = "challenge"` through a
dialogue choice) once the Warden's Trial is done; the other four are a
choice on their fight's own offer (`challenge = ...` beside `battle` /
`boss`), so the challenge applies to that fight.

Rest points (`kind = "rest"`, with a save) stand on the 1F stair landing,
by the 5F hearth and in a 7F alcove off the landing.

Quest and boss rewards hand out cards by id from `cards.toml`, among them
the four legendaries.

### Modes

The Gambler's Rest's five tables are `modes.toml` instances, and the
keeper's quests count wins at each by id:

Tower Game Night ends on a podium in the Rest's hall: the top three's
leaders on 2nd / 1st / 3rd blocks, the rivals played by the Rest's
regulars, confetti and a slow shot round them (`modes.toml` `podium`).

- **Tower High Table** (`tower-high-table`): six-seat no-limit Hold'em for
  gold, 5,000 buy-in, expert opponents, blinds doubling every eight hands.
- **The Warden's Duel** (`wardens-duel`): a Grid Duel against the tower's
  own breed, with elemental cells, chain captures and stakes, played at the
  card room's table on the 5F floor: the Warden's second across the board,
  two regulars watching, the tower's card dealer beside them (talk to the
  second to sit down).
- **The Genesis Links** (`genesis-links`): six holes - bunkers guarding a
  green, a dogleg, an island green behind a bridge, stepped terraces
  (height grid), conveyor ramps round a wall (slope tiles), and a long par
  5 to a green that slopes away.
- **The Monastery Run** (`spiral-circuit`): a sprint for six expert racers
  across Drake's overworld (`map01`), from the water gate's southern landing
  to the Biron Monastery through twelve checkpoint gates, with nine
  power-ups along the way.
  Picking it at the table takes the party out onto the overworld, and back
  to the 5F when the race is over.
- **The Old Vault** (`old-vault`): six-player prop hunt, two hunters, among
  urns, crates, chests and braziers between pillar rows.

Once the keeper has welcomed the party, the 5F card room and games room
offer every table through dialogue choices (`mode = ...`), and the High
Table's empty seat deals in on a step (`kind = "mode"`). Two more instances
play on the tower itself, in the 3D field: **Tower Green** (`tower-green`),
one hole across the 1F dais, and **Sol Ring** (`sol-ring`), three laps of
the 1F floor round the dais; both open from the mode picker.

Sol Ring stays in the tower as its short warm-up circuit; the long races
run on the overworld, where there is room to run to. **Drake Dash**
(`drake-circuit`) is the gentler of the two: four racers from the fields
under Rim Elm to the water gate, a hairpin to cut with a hop and a boost
lying off the plain's long straight for whoever hopped to it.

The earlier village instances (`mist-lantern-table`, `haven-duel`,
`windmill-links`, `drake-circuit`, `storehouse`) stay as the gentler set.

### Gear

`items.toml` is the gear worth chasing between 60 and 99 (the format is
[`expansion-pack-items.md`](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack-items.md)).
Retail's best is the Ra-Seru set; the Vigil set sits about 12-15% above
it a piece and rewards wearing it together.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| 5F Tower Armory, from the start | Tower Draught (2,500 HP), Mist Tonic (300 MP), Phoenix Plume (party revive at 50%), Healing Berry, the Warden Mail / Robe / Plate (body armour between Triumph and Ra-Seru) |
| Armory, after the Verdant Colossus | Sovereign Nectar (full HP, party), Ysolde's Seal (Master Guard + HP Boost 1) |
| Armory, after the Engine Deep | Tower Sigil (AP Boost 2 + HP After) |
| Armory, after the Iron Regent | Vigil Mail / Robe / Plate (UDF/LDF 86-96 against Ra-Seru's 75-84) and the Vigil Crown (UDF 71, INT 70) |
| Armory, after the Azure Seraph | Vigil Greaves (ATK 98, LDF 70, SPD 35 against Ra-Seru Thongs 88/64/32) |
| Boss rewards | Cinder Warden: Ember Heart (Fire Guard, +15 ATK). Verdant Colossus: Vigil Maul (Gala, ATK 114 against the Ra-Seru Club's 100). Iron Regent: Vigil Blade (Vahn, 112 against 98). Azure Seraph: Vigil Talon (Noa, 110 against 96). Hollow Sovereign: Sovereign's Eye (Attack x2 + Arts Power). |
| Quests and drops | Every Floor: the Mist Lantern (EXP Boost + Items Up, for the climb to 99). A Remedy for Stone: two Phoenix Plumes. Throne Heralds drop Phoenix Plumes; Storm Giliums can be robbed of Mist Tonics. |

The Vigil set (each hero's weapon and body armour, the crown, the greaves)
adds +10 ATK at two pieces, +12 UDF and LDF at three and All Guard at four.
Open the bag from the Journal's Items page; the Gear tab shows each stat
before and after a piece goes on.

## Levelling to 99: the numbers

**The curve.** Retail asks for 9.65 million XP to reach 99, 7.5 million of
it past level 60. `progression.toml` keeps retail's steps through 39 (the
story) and cuts each later step in bands (x0.75 at 40 down to x0.3 at 90),
so every level from 40 to 99 costs between about 36,000 and 90,000 XP and
the cost rises steadily: 60 to 99 is **2,492,187 XP** per character.

**A fight's EXP.** A won battle sums its monsters' EXP; the pack's enemy
scaling multiplies it (and the monsters' stats) by `1 + 0.5% x (party level
- 50)`, at most x1.25 - slower than the party itself grows, so a level gained
is a level that counts. `xp_mul` adds half again, and the retail victory
share gives each of three living members a quarter of the pool:

```text
share = sum(monster exp) x scale(level) x 1.5 x 3/4 / 3
```

**The curve, checked.** `crates/engine-expansion/tests/rebirth_balance.rs`
seats every pack formation the way the engine does (`derive_monster`, the
level scaling, the battle loader's install profile), runs both sides' hits
through the melee kernel (`physical_predamage`) and holds each fight to a
target at Normal, Hard and Nightmare; the model's assumptions are in the
file's header. `rebirth_chain.rs` plays the whole quest chain through the
tracker. At Normal, at the level each area is first met:

| Area | Fight | Level | Rounds to win | Rounds survived unhealed | Worst move | Fights per level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Isles | `isles_shore` | 30 | 3.4 | 9.7 | 122 | 6.1 |
| Isles | Thornwood Queen | 35 | 7.5 | 4.4 | 980 | 3.4 |
| 1F | `forge_guard` | 40 | 4.1 | 9.0 | 145 | 4.3 |
| 1F | Tower Gauntlet | 45 | 9.1 | 13.3 | 145 | 1.8 |
| 2F | Cinder Warden | 50 | 9.0 | 6.5 | 1,114 | 1.9 |
| 3F | `mire_bloom` | 55 | 4.6 | 10.6 | 170 | 3.2 |
| 3F | Garden Gauntlet | 60 | 12.7 | 14.5 | 167 | 1.2 |
| 4F | `fountain_court` | 60 | 4.7 | 10.2 | 187 | 2.8 |
| 4F | Verdant Colossus | 65 | 9.8 | 6.4 | 785 | 1.7 |
| 6F | `storm_engine` | 70 | 4.9 | 7.4 | 286 | 2.5 |
| 6F | Iron Regent | 75 | 11.8 | 4.3 | 1,314 | 1.3 |
| 7F | `prism_storm` | 80 | 3.9 | 7.6 | 461 | 3.0 |
| 7F | Azure Seraph | 85 | 11.1 | 6.0 | 1,874 | 1.9 |
| 8F | `herald_watch` | 90 | 4.5 | 7.2 | 470 | 2.9 |
| 8F | Hollow Sovereign | 90 | 14.7 | 3.5 | 1,514 | 1.0 |
| 8F | Echo of the Throne | 95 | 10.2 | 6.5 | 734 | 1.6 |
| 8F | Echo Storm (x1.5) | 99 | 14.4 | 3.5 | 1,411 | - |
| 1F | The First Breath | 99 | 15.3 | 4.7 | 2,620 | - |

Field fights last three to five rounds and move the bar every three to six
of them; a keeper or gauntlet is worth a level or more. Hard (enemy stats
x1.35, attacks x1.25) stretches the keepers to 12-20 rounds; Nightmare
(x1.8, x1.5) to 16-23, with the party lasting about one round unhealed
against the superbosses - winnable with Spirit and healing, and no single
blow at any preset lands for a full-HP member's whole HP.

**Rewards on the way.** Level 55 brings the tower's arts and a Power and
Guardian Water, 80 the Knell finishers, 99 the Warden's last request and
the First Breath; the gear chase runs from the Ra-Seru set through the
Vigil set (see Gear).

## Playing it

The pack needs your own Legend of Legaia (NA) disc; it carries no game data.

In play, the tower is entered from the retail game: once the party reaches
level 30, the tiles behind the woodpile by Rim Elm's south gate (`town01`,
field-grid tiles 17-18 x 43) lead up into the Atrium - the 1F map's
`[[entrances]]` table - and the Atrium's stair down returns beside them. The
Journal's Travel page returns to any of the pack's maps the party has been
to, from anywhere, and offers the Atrium itself once the party reaches level
30 (`--cheat-travel` lists every map, for testing).

```bash
# Validate (no disc needed)
asset expansion validate packs/rebirth

# Native window: enter the tower's first floor directly
legaia-engine play-window --disc "Legend of Legaia (USA).bin" \
    --expansion packs/rebirth --map genesis_1f
```

## How it was built

Rebirth is meant to be read as the example of the workbench and format, so
here is how each part came together.

**Choosing base scenes.** Each kept floor is a retail room re-purposed: the
modder screenshots candidate scenes (`play-window --scene <name>
--screenshot`), picks one that reads as a tower floor, and lays the map over
it with `geometry = "keep"`. The base scene's meshes, textures and ground
draw as on the disc; the pack supplies the walls, zones and exits.

**Re-tracing the walls.** A kept room only walks the way it looks if the
pack's wall quarters match the room. The workbench's Maps tab paints them
over the base scene's own layout; for Rebirth the rows were traced from each
room's retail collision grid (wall quarters and floor tiers), flood-filled
from the floor's centre so only the room itself is floor, and every tile
outside it painted as a solid wall that keeps the retail floor tier. That last
part matters on a terraced scene: the ground's corner heights read the tiers
of the tiles around them ([the corner rule](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack-maps.md#tiers-are-corner-heights)),
so a terrace at tier 8 next to a tier-0 wall drops into a spike. 4F keeps
every surrounding tier for that reason.

**Built from scratch.** The 1F Atrium is the other style: `geometry = "none"`,
floor textures named by atlas cell (`ground = { kind = "texture" }`) or
borrowed from a base cell, and props from the base scene's geometry pack.
The workbench's `scene_objects` view lists each mesh's footprint; mesh 20 is
an octagonal pillar about two tiles across (placed at `scale = 0.6`), mesh 19
a carved face pillar, mesh 37 a stone altar block (the Warden's Stone).

**NPCs without models.** A pack NPC is a talk zone: stepping onto the tiles in
front of the Warden's Stone raises `talk tower_guide`, which is what a quest's
`giver` and `talk` objective listen for. Most bosses are a quest whose
`start_dialog` and `active_dialog` is a line with a fight choice, so the
player can step back from a fight and return to it. The Iron Regent's quest
also asks for the Engine Gauntlet, so his offer is a trigger of its own,
gated on him still standing (`requires = { bosses_unbeaten = [...] }`); a
second trigger on the same tiles says an after line once he has fallen
(`requires = { bosses = [...] }`), as on every boss floor.

**Monsters.** Every monster is a retail one renumbered: the workbench's
Battle tab picks the base from the disc catalog and shows its retail stats
beside each field. Bases were checked in a battle screenshot before use
(`play-window --battle cell:s:<hex id>`): the Juggernaut-form Cort (181)
draws nothing on an ordinary stage, so the superboss's second phase is built
on Songi (179) instead.

**Sound.** Every floor keeps a retail track by its sound-test id; the
map `[audio]` tables add the rest
([`expansion-pack-audio.md`](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack-audio.md)).
5F's games room is a music zone on the Sol casino's "Wild Declaration", so
the bar tune cross-fades into it at the door; 7F's inner sanctum hands the
music to the pack's own drone, a six-second loop of whole-cycle sine partials
that carries its loop in its WAV `smpl` chunk. The ember crystals (1F), the
braziers and the fire at their middle (2F), the Rest's hearth (5F) and the
throne's standing lamps (8F) crackle, the Warden's Stone hums and
water runs in the garden's channels (3F), each a positional source heard by
distance and panned across the view. The Hollow Sovereign opens on "Apostles
of the Mist", turns to "Apocalypse" as its shell cracks, rings a chime as it
is unmade and on every Grand Beam telegraph, and its unbound form arrives to
the Wild Arms battle theme. The Rest's crowd murmurs, loudest by the
tables (5F); the engine hums at both flywheels (6F); the sunken court drips
(4F); a fountain plays in the garden (3F); and the wind howls through the
open top (8F). The WAV files are synthesised from sine
partials and seeded noise by `scripts/models/generate_rebirth_audio.py`; no
disc audio is copied.

## No game data

The pack ships no bytes from the disc. Every monster, mesh, texture, scene or
music cue it uses is a coordinate the engine resolves against the player's
own copy, so the pack is safe to share. The validator enforces it.

## Gaps

The gaps found while building this pack - arming a challenge, entering a
mode from a map, gated exits, triggers and NPC lines, rest points - are
format features now ([`expansion-pack-maps.md`](../../docs/formats/expansion-pack-maps.md#gates)).
Above 1F the stairs stay open by choice: the quest chain paces the climb by level.

Every pack flag and counter the pack writes is read somewhere (the
validator's flow lints hold it to that): the trial's `tower_open` lifts the
stair seal and arms the dais guardian, `rest_open` opens the 5F tables,
`hollow_heard`, `tables_beaten`, `sovereign_fallen` and `breath_released`
turn NPC lines, `throne_broken` and `vigil_kept` gate the last two quests, the
Isles flags gate the next Isles quest and Pell's late stock, and the
`bosses_felled`, `bounties` and `echoes_broken` counters are objectives of
**The Last Vigil**, **Tower Bounty Hunter** and **Echo Breaker**.

# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - cutscenes.
#
# Scripted scenes on the tower's maps: the steps of each run on the
# engine's cutscene sequencer (a camera move, a walk, a line, a fade) one
# after another, with the `tracks` running beside the main list.
# Format: docs/formats/expansion-pack-cutscenes.md.
#
# Map tiles here are each map's own: `[column, row]` from the top-left of
# its `tiles.rows`.

# --- 1F: the tower wakes ------------------------------------------------------

# The first arrival in the Atrium (maps/genesis_1f.toml
# `enter_cutscenes`): the camera rises up the hall toward the stair above,
# the Warden's familiar pads down off the dais to meet the party, and
# Ysolde's voice calls them to the stone. It leaves the party where it
# arrived, so stepping toward the dais still raises the stone's own talk
# (`tower_rumour`). One line is said: the shot and the familiar carry the
# rest.
[cutscenes.tower_intro]
title = "The Tower Wakes"
map = "genesis_1f"
letterbox = true

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "fade"
to = "black"

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "camera"
focus = { tile = [7, 11] }
pitch = -14.0
zoom = 0.55

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "fade"
to = "clear"
frames = 60

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "start_track"
track = "crane"

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "wait"
frames = 150

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "join"
track = "crane"

# The stone stirs.
[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "shake"
amplitude = 10
frames = 50

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "flash"
color = [70, 90, 140]
frames = 30

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "show"
npc = "warden_familiar"
tile = [5, 4]

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "camera"
focus = { actor = "warden_familiar" }
pitch = 6.0
zoom = 1.25
frames = 70

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "move"
actor = "warden_familiar"
path = [[5, 8], [6, 9]]

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "face"
actor = "warden_familiar"
toward = "player"

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "face"
actor = "player"
toward = "warden_familiar"

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "camera"
focus = { tile = [7, 6] }
pitch = 4.0
zoom = 1.45
frames = 90

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "flash"
color = [90, 120, 190]
frames = 40

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "say"
line = "intro_voice"

# The familiar goes back up to wait by the dais; the shot comes home.
[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "move"
actor = "warden_familiar"
to = [4, 8]
wait = false

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "camera_reset"
frames = 60

[[cutscenes.tower_intro.steps]]
do = "face"
actor = "warden_familiar"
facing = 4

# The crane up the hall: from low over the entrance up to the stair at the
# far end, pulling back as it rises.
[[cutscenes.tower_intro.tracks.crane.steps]]
do = "camera"
focus = { tile = [7, 3] }
pitch = 24.0

# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - dialogue.
#
# Each line of `text` is one row of the dialog box; a blank line starts a
# new page. Rows are short: retail boxes do not wrap, and the validator
# warns past 36 characters.
# Format: docs/formats/expansion-pack-quests.md.
#
# The tower's guide is Warden Ysolde, last of the Genesis Wardens: an
# order of island root-tenders who kept the old root under the tower long
# before they hung a bell over it. When the Mist came she sealed its first
# breath under the Warden's Stone and bound herself into the stone to hold
# it there; she speaks through it on the first floor. Every word here is
# the pack's own, original fan writing that quotes no retail line.
#
# The Genesis Trees' deep history (the roots that run tree to tree under
# land and sea, the oldest of them under the tower, the rootlight shrubs
# that drink from a root near the surface, why the Mist never took the
# isles) is told in pieces the player can walk past: Ysolde's journal
# pages on the floors, the Atrium murals, Imre the scholar in Tolva's
# Haven, rootlight shrubs, and the grotto where the root comes up. Every
# one is an examined object (`press = true`) or an NPC's idle line, so none
# of it stops the player. It stands beside the retail story: the Trees push
# the Mist back, and nothing here says what the Mist is.

# --- The Warden's Stone (1F) -------------------------------------------------

[lines.guide_intro]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
...So the stone wakes. I am
Ysolde, last Warden of Genesis.

The bell above has been silent
since the Mist. What it took is
here now. Will you hear it?"""

[lines.guide_trial]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
Win three battles and reach
level 40. Then come back to me.

The sea gate in the west wall
leads to the Lantern Isles."""

[lines.guide_trial_active]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
Three battles, and level 40.
The sea gate west will help."""

[lines.guide_done]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
Yes... you will do. The seal is
lifted, and eight floors await.

The fire on the second floor
wakes at level 50. Climb well."""

[lines.guide_vigil_done]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
There is nothing more the tower
can teach you.

Under this stone lies the Mist's
first breath. I have held it so
long I forget what hands are.

You can meet it now, and I can
finally let go. Stand ready."""

[lines.gauntlet_offer]
speaker = "The Bell"
text = """
A bronze bell. Ring it, and the
tower sends its first breed."""
choices = [
    { label = "Ring the bell.", battle = "tower_gauntlet" },
    { label = "Leave it.", reply = "The bell sways, and is still." },
]

# --- The First Breath (1F, past level 99) -------------------------------------

[lines.breath_offer]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
When I lift the seal, it comes
up all at once. That is yours."""
choices = [
    { label = "Lift the seal.", boss = "first_breath" },
    { label = "Not yet.", reply = "Then I hold it a little longer.\nI am good at that." },
]

[lines.breath_done]
speaker = "Warden Ysolde"
text = """
...Do you hear it? The bell.
First time since the Mist came.

The watch is kept. I can let go
now. Thank you, all of you."""

[lines.breath_wind]
text = "The Breath turns to a howling gale!"

[lines.breath_thunder]
text = "The heralds answer the Breath!"

[lines.breath_charge]
text = "The whole hall breathes in..."

[lines.breath_end]
text = "The stone shudders under it!"

[lines.breath_last]
text = "It will not be held. It will not!"

# --- Genesis Tree lore (examined objects and NPC lines) ----------------------
#
# Each is meant for a `press = true` dialog trigger on a map, or an NPC's
# `line`: something the player chooses to look at. Shown in any order, they
# tell one history; none depends on another.

# Rootlight: green shrubs that drink from a root running near the surface
# and glow with it. The generic line, for any glowing shrub.
[lines.rootlight_shrub]
text = """
(A low green shrub, lit from
inside. The glow swells and
fades, slow as a sleeper.)

(The islanders call it rootlight.)"""

# The rootlight round the Warden's Stone (1F), thickest in the pack.
[lines.rootlight_stone]
text = """
(Rootlight grows thick here,
pressed close around the stone,
as if to keep it warm.)"""

# The Atrium murals (1F): three panels, oldest to newest.
[lines.mural_roots]
speaker = "Atrium Mural"
text = """
(A worn mural. Robed figures
kneel around a great root with
ladles, watering it.)

(Above them, very small, a tree
so tall it leaves the frame.)"""

[lines.mural_stone]
speaker = "Atrium Mural"
text = """
(Masons cut a block from the
root itself. It has turned to
stone, but they lift it gently.)

(Carved under it: GENESIS.)"""

[lines.mural_bell]
speaker = "Atrium Mural"
text = """
(The newest panel. A bronze bell
hangs over the stone, and boats
turn home through the fog.)"""

# Ysolde's journal, one page on each of five floors (2F, 3F, 4F, 6F, 7F)
# and the last at the throne (8F, once it is empty).
[lines.journal_2f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(A page in a careful hand.)

Old Hesk took me under the floor
today, to the root. He says we
tended roots before we rang bells.

The bell only calls the boats
home, he says. The root is the
watch."""

[lines.journal_3f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(A page, pressed between leaves.)

Planted rootlight on the cliff
path. Where it takes, the fog
thins. Hesk says it always has."""

[lines.journal_4f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(A page, green with moss.)

Hesk's tale: every Genesis Tree
reaches for the others, root to
root, under the sea and stone.

Ours is the oldest root. Cut a
stone from it, the first Wardens
said, and build on the tree."""

[lines.journal_6f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(A page, smudged with grease.)

The bell engine jammed again. I
rang it by hand all night. My
arms will forgive me.

The boats came home."""

[lines.journal_7f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(A page, the ink run with damp.)

Fog off the sea, but not fog. It
does not lift at noon. The boats
do not answer the bell.

The Trees inland have gone quiet.
Only our root still breathes. I
know what I have to do."""

[lines.journal_8f]
speaker = "Ysolde's Journal"
text = """
(The last page.)

I will go into the stone, and
hold the breath there, over the
root. The Mist cannot sit on it.

Whoever reads this: ring the bell
when it is over. I would like to
hear it once more."""

# Imre, a scholar from the mainland, in Tolva's Haven: `line`, then
# `line_after` once the Pearl has been heard (`isles_pearl_heard`).
[lines.isles_scholar]
speaker = "Scholar Imre"
text = """
Mind the shrubs! Sorry. I am
Imre. I study the Genesis Trees.

Everyone knows the Trees push the
Mist back. Nobody asks what they
do underground.

Roots, I think, tree to tree. And
rootlight grows right over them."""

[lines.isles_scholar_after]
speaker = "Scholar Imre"
text = """
The grotto root runs east, under
the sea, straight to the tower.

So the old tale is true. Genesis
Tower stands on the oldest root
there is. I need a bigger book."""

# Where the root breaks through in the Singing Grotto, by the Pearl's pool.
[lines.grotto_root]
speaker = "The Root"
text = """
(A root as thick as a ferry hull
breaks from the cave wall and
dips into the pool.)

(It is warm. Rootlight moss grows
thick along it, and it beats
under your hand, slow as breath.)

(It runs east, under the sea,
toward the tower.)"""

# Genesis Tower, first floor: the Atrium. Unlike the floors above, this
# one is laid out from scratch (`geometry = "none"`): a walled hall with a
# raised dais floating in the dark, built from the retail Sky Gardens
# Tower's (`tower`) textures and meshes. The Warden's Stone stands on the
# dais, ringed by rootlight, with daylight falling on it from the high
# windows; the stair at the south edge leads back down to Rim Elm, the one
# at the north edge up into the tower. East of the dais a narrow bridge
# crosses the root shaft - the well the Genesis root climbs through the
# tower's core, glowing green far below - into the Hall of Trials: the
# gauntlet bell in its niche, the trial obelisk in the middle of the floor,
# and the card dealer's stall against the far wall - each a place the party
# walks to, not a tile it trips over.

name = "Genesis Tower 1F - Atrium"
size = [29, 13]
base = { scene = { kind = "scene", name = "tower" }, geometry = "none" }
# Sound-test track 25, "The Quiet Genesis Tree": the stone was cut from a
# root of the first one, and the Atrium is where the party comes to rest.
bgm = { kind = "bgm", id = 25 }
camera = "default"
# Tier 0 is the Atrium floor, tier 1 the dais and the Hall of Trials, tier
# 2 the bell niche. Tiers are corner heights, so the gallery's last row of
# cells is a ramp up into the hall and the niche's rim slopes down to it.
floor_heights = [0, 48, 96]

# The Atrium floats in the dark: past its parapet the hall's stone falls
# away to a floor far below, and the tower's outer wall stands round it on
# every side but the camera's, so the view over the south parapet ends on
# stone fading into the dark rather than on the clear colour. The void
# between the Atrium and the Hall of Trials is the root shaft (the region
# below): its walls go down much further, into black, and the bridge
# crosses it.
[surround]
ground = { tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 }
side = { tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 2 }
depth = 448
shade = 40
fade = 12
backdrop = { tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 2, height = 1152, distance = 2, shade = 72 }

[[surround.regions]]
rect = [15, 0, 18, 12]   # the root shaft
depth = 2048
shade = 48
fade = 4

# The vault overhead: the gauntlet bell hang on chains from it. The follow camera
# looks down from under it, so only the chains show, rising out of the
# frame; the underside is wound to face down and drawn only from beneath.
[ceiling]
height = 2048
cell = { tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 2 }
shade = 40
chain = { tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 2, width = 6, shade = 72, items = ["gauntlet_bell"] }

[tiles]
origin = [16, 16]
rows = [
  "#######<#######   ___________",
  "#....bj.jb....#   #:k:NBN:k:%",
  "#.o.,.,.,.,.o.#   #:O:NNN:O:%",
  "#.............#   #:::::::::%",
  "#,...^^^^^...,#    :::::::::%",
  "#....^^^^^.....    :::::::::%",
  "w,.o.^^^^^.o...----....T::::%",
  "#....^^^^^.....    :::::::::%",
  "#,...^^^^^...,#    :::::::::%",
  "#.............#   #:::::::::%",

[tiles.legend]
# The walls stand: the Sky Gardens Tower's own tile-sized stone block
# (mesh 10, three storeys) on the north, east and west, and a low generated
# parapet along the south so the follow camera sees over it. The Hall of
# Trials turns that round: the follow camera looks south from its north
# side, so the hall and the gallery keep the low parapet on the camera's
# side and the tall stone on the far side, where it closes the room in.
# The hall's east and south walls stand on its raised floor (`%`), so the
# floor stays level up to them rather than sloping down at the rim.
"#" = { label = "wall", walls = "all", wall = { kind = "mesh", index = 10 } }
"%" = { label = "wall (hall)", height = 1, walls = "all", wall = { kind = "mesh", index = 10 } }
"_" = { label = "parapet", walls = "all", wall = { kind = "box", height = 96, tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 2 } }
"." = { label = "stone floor", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
"," = { label = "worn stone", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
"^" = { label = "dais", height = 1, ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 0 } }
":" = { label = "hall floor", height = 1, ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
"N" = { label = "bell niche", height = 2, ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 0 } }
"B" = { label = "under the bell", height = 2, ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 0 } }
# Pillar and statue bases: solid, the floor under them. The columns
# themselves are decorations (below), so each can carry a cap.
"o" = { label = "pillar base", walls = "all", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
"O" = { label = "pillar base (hall)", height = 1, walls = "all", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
# Brazier stands (`models/brazier.glb` props): solid.
"j" = { label = "brazier", walls = "all", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
"k" = { label = "brazier (hall)", height = 1, walls = "all", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
# The trial obelisk and the card dealer's stall: solid.
"T" = { label = "trial obelisk", height = 1, walls = "all", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
"c" = { label = "stall plants", height = 1, walls = "all", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
"x" = { label = "stall counter", height = 1, walls = "all", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }
# Where the stair-up banners hang: stone floor the wall edges leave bare.
"b" = { label = "banner spot", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
"=" = { label = "stair landing", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
# The bridge over the root shaft: the dais's own flagstones, nothing either
# side of it but the drop.
"-" = { label = "shaft bridge", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 0 } }
">" = { label = "stair down", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
"<" = { label = "stair up", ground = { kind = "base_cell", cell = [8, 11] } }
# The sea gate: a crack in the west wall, salt wind and a stair down to
# the Lantern Isles (maps/isles_beach.toml).
"w" = { label = "sea gate", ground = { kind = "texture", tpage = 28, clut = 32576, tile = 1 } }

# (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Rogue's Tower (`rugi`) brick and
# rock: a stair of fire that climbs away from the camera, landing over
# landing, above the lava lake far down the tower's core. The landing opens
# on the lower hall, its centre aisle cut from the side aisles by two
# chasms with a bridge across each, the lake's glow coming up through them;
# off the hall, the west forge (anvils and a slag trough) and the east ash
# shrine. The first flight climbs to the middle landing, a span of stone
# with nothing either side of it but the drop and four ember pillars on it;
# the second to the upper terrace, where the Cinder Warden's brazier burns
# on a raised dais and the stair up leaves through the far wall behind it.
#

# edge is a low parapet, its far and side walls stand full height.

# Genesis Tower, third floor: the Hanging Garden. Laid out from scratch
# (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Sky Gardens' (`teien`) flagstones,
# lawns, hedges and brick arches: three terraces stepping up away from the
# camera. The lower garden opens off the landing, its flower beds and
# hedge blocks round a fountain. A flight climbs to the middle terrace: the
# orchard to the west (where the Gilded Herd grazes), the rose arbour's
# arches to the east, and between them the garden well - a deep green pit
# down the tower's core, the root glowing at its foot - with the sundial
# plaza standing in it on its own pillar of stone, four narrow walks out to
# it. The plaza runs the Garden Gauntlet. A second flight climbs to the
# upper terrace: a lawn
# round a reflecting basin, the belvedere on the east edge open to the sky
# past a low balustrade, and the stair up under an arch in the far wall.
#
# The follow camera looks south from the north side: each terrace's north
# edge is a low balustrade, its far and side edges hedge or stone walls.

size = [39, 40]
base = { scene = { kind = "scene", name = "teien" }, geometry = "none" }
# Sound-test track 2, "Winds, Trees and Water": a garden at rest.
bgm = { kind = "bgm", id = 2 }
camera = "far"
# Tier 0 the landing and lower garden, tier 1 the middle terrace and the
# walks over the well, tier 2 the sundial plaza and upper terrace, tier 3
# the belvedere. Each walk's last tile before the plaza ramps up to it.

# Genesis Tower, fourth floor: the Verdant Vault. Laid out from scratch
# (`geometry = "none"`) out of present-day Conkram's (`concnow`) veined
# green stone, carved white marble, columns, planters and roots: a vault
# the party climbs down into. The stair from below opens on a high gallery
# that rings the vault; stairs drop from it to the colonnade, and steps
# drop again into the sunken court at the centre, where the moss over the
# Verdant Colossus breathes round four flooded corners. Off the west
# gallery, the Root Archive: its floor long since fallen into the dark, four
# root trunks of the Genesis root rising out of the pit, and the Wardens'
# narrow walks still running between them; off the east, the Flooded
# Cloister a step down, its pools full of rainwater. The stair up leaves
# from the south gallery.
#

# is a low parapet, the vault's far and side walls stand full height.

# Genesis Tower, fifth floor: the Gambler's Rest. Laid out from scratch
# (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Sol Tower rooms' (`koin1`) dark
# planks, brick and furniture. No monster climbs this high, and the Rest
# is the tower's one warm floor, built on three levels: the stair from
# below opens on a gallery over the hall, a grand stair runs down into it,
# and past the bar a balustrade looks down on the sunken lounge, where the
# piano plays on its stage and the stair up leaves. In the hall Keeper
# Odalric pours behind the long bar, the regulars wait round the High
# Table and the hearth burns on the east wall (rest and save). Off the
# hall, the card room to the west (the Warden's Duel table and the tower's
# card dealer) and the games room to the east (Tower Game Night, the
# arcade cabinets, its own music).
#
# The follow camera looks south from the north side: each room's north
# edge is a low rail, the far and side walls stand full height, and from
# the gallery it looks down over the whole hall.

size = [37, 30]
base = { scene = { kind = "scene", name = "koin1" }, geometry = "none" }

camera = "far"
# Three levels: the sunken lounge (tier 0, its stage tier 1), the hall and
# its side rooms (tier 2), and the gallery the stair from below opens on
# (tier 6), a grand stair (tiers 5, 4) down into the hall and a short flight
# (tier 3) on down to the lounge.

# Genesis Tower, sixth floor: the Engine Deep. Laid out from scratch
# (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Jette's Fortress (`chitei2`)
# marble, riveted plate and machinery: the engine that once turned the
# bell fills a shaft sunk deep into the tower, and the floor is the iron
# decks hung over it. Two long walkways run down the shaft's sides, a
# gantry runs down its middle, and two bridges cross it; far below, the
# engine's great wheels still turn in the furnace glow. Off the walkways'
# middle, the control room (west), where the lever starts the Engine
# Gauntlet, and the furnace room (east). The Iron Regent holds the dais at
# the gantry's end, an island over the pit with his flywheels turning
# either side of it; the stair up leaves from the end of the east walkway.
#
# The follow camera looks south from the north side: the shaft's and the
# side rooms' north walls are low, so the camera sees in over them and
# down into the pit.

name = "Genesis Tower 6F - Engine Deep"
size = [35, 37]
base = { scene = { kind = "scene", name = "chitei2" }, geometry = "none" }
# Sound-test track 13, "Bio-Castle".
bgm = { kind = "bgm", id = 13 }
camera = "far"
# Tier 1 the decks, side rooms and the Regent's dais, tier 2 the Regent's
# own step. Nothing walks tier 0: it is only the height the pit's depth is
# measured from.
floor_heights = [0, 64, 112]

# The pit: the shaft's walls drop far below the decks to the engine floor
# at its foot, dim in the furnace glow.
[surround]
ground = { tpage = 9, clut = 31110, tile = 19 }
side = { tpage = 9, clut = 31176, tile = 3 }
depth = 1280
shade = 40
# The walls darken as they go down, into the dark at the foot.
fade = 8
# The tower's outer wall stands round the drop on every side but the
# camera's, so the view over the far walls ends on stone, fading into the
# dark, rather than on the clear colour.
backdrop = { tpage = 8, clut = 30979, tile = 27, height = 1152, distance = 2, shade = 96 }

# The shaft itself: its floor, the engine's bed, lies shallower than the
# drop past the tower's walls, so the cogs on it stay in the follow
# camera's view over the decks' rims.
[[surround.regions]]
rect = [11, 5, 23, 35]
depth = 640

# Genesis Tower, seventh floor: the Sanctum of Echoes. Laid out from
# scratch (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Sol Tower vault's
# (`korb3`) pale stone and blue steel. The sea came into the tower here
# long ago and stayed: the whole floor is still water, and the octagon is
# walked on boardwalks laid round its walls. The stair from below opens on
# a landing at the ring's north point, with a quiet rest alcove off it; a
# stone causeway runs from the landing across the water to the walled
# inner sanctum, an island where the Azure Seraph keeps the raised heart;
# four echo shrines stand on the boardwalk in the ring's diagonal bays,
# two jetties run out into the water at the ring's east and west points,
# and the stair up leaves from the ring's south point. The islanders say
# the drowned sailors' prayers settled on this floor; lanterns float on the
# water for them.
#
# The follow camera looks south from the north side: the outer ring's north
# walls and the sanctum's north wall are low, so the camera sees into the
# rooms over them; the sanctum's south wall is half height, so the camera
# keeps the party in view walking the south arc behind it.

# Tier 0 is the boardwalk ring and the causeway, tier 1 the sanctum,

# Genesis Tower, eighth floor: the Hollow Throne. The summit is laid out
# from scratch (`geometry = "none"`) out of the retail Zora's Floating
# Castle's (`taiku2`) stone, carpet and carved throne: the stair from below
# opens on a landing and a narthex runs the width of the tower. Past the
# nave's door the floor is gone: the long red carpet runs on as a bridge
# over the open shaft of the tower, crossed halfway by a causeway to the two
# chapels - the Hall of Fallen Crowns to the west, its obelisks dark, and
# the Broken Gallery to the east, its outer wall gone and the wind coming
# through. The throne stands on its dais at the bridge's end, an island
# over the drop with the night sky open round it, and behind it, out over
# the abyss on its own pier, the tower's great bell hangs silent in its
# yoke. No encounters on the landing: the long walk over the carpet is the
# build-up to the floor's only fight, the superboss in two waves
# (battle.toml, `hollow_throne`).
#
# The follow camera looks south from the north side, so every room's north
# edge (the side the camera stands on) is a low parapet and its south and
# side walls stand full height; the throne and the bell sit at the south
# end, ahead of the party all the way over the bridge.

name = "Genesis Tower 8F - Hollow Throne"
size = [31, 39]
base = { scene = { kind = "scene", name = "taiku2" }, geometry = "none" }
# Sound-test track 52, "Ominous Presence".
bgm = { kind = "bgm", id = 52 }
camera = "far"
# Tier 0 is the hall floor and the bridge, tier 1 the dais and the
# chapels and the bell's pier, tier 2 the throne's own step. Tiers are
# corner heights, so each raised block's edge cells are its steps.
floor_heights = [0, 40, 80]

# The shaft of the tower: castle stone falling away into the dark, so far
# down its foot is only a dim floor of the flagstones below.
[surround]
ground = { tpage = 24, clut = 31170, tile = 3 }
side = { tpage = 24, clut = 31168, tile = 0 }
depth = 2048
shade = 32
# The tower's outer wall rises only on the west, behind the Hall of Fallen
# Crowns; to the east and south the summit is open to the night sky.
backdrop = { tpage = 24, clut = 31168, tile = 0, height = 1152, distance = 2, sides = "w", shade = 96 }
# The shaft's walls darken into the dark below.
fade = 4

# The vault overhead: the narthex lanterns hang on chains from it. The follow camera
# looks down from under it, so only the chains show, rising out of the
# frame; the underside is wound to face down and drawn only from beneath.
[ceiling]
height = 2048
cell = { tpage = 24, clut = 31168, tile = 0 }
shade = 40
chain = { tpage = 24, clut = 31168, tile = 0, width = 6, shade = 72, items = ["narthex_lantern_1", "narthex_lantern_2", "narthex_lantern_3", "narthex_lantern_4"] }

# Snowdrift Cave's (`cave01`) rock round a great hollow: the stair comes down
# into the antechamber, and from its lip a stone causeway runs out over the
# drop to the Landing, the crown of a rock pillar halfway across. From there

# Lantern Isles: the Thornwood. Laid out over the West Voz Forest (`vell`)
# as a walk with a shape: the lane leaves the village's fields at the wood's
# edge and winds east under clumped old growth - through Mushroom Hollow, a
# sunken glade ringed with toadstools; over the brook's gorge on a plank
# footbridge, the water running far below; up to the old shrine, a broken
# ring of standing stones round an inscribed tablet, with a spur climbing
# to a lookout high over the canopy; down to the
# hermit's camp, pitched round the log he sits on; and on to the island's
# ruined court, where the Thornwood Queen has grown her hive inside the

# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - the flagship expansion pack.
#
# Authored with the same format and tooling any modder uses
# (docs/formats/expansion-pack.md). Content sections (battle.toml,
# quests.toml, maps/, ...) are added beside this file as they are written.

id = "rebirth"
name = "Legend of Legaia: Rebirth"
# The launcher's Expansion button and other narrow places.
short_name = "Rebirth"
version = "0.2.0"
authors = ["The legend-of-legaia-re contributors"]
license = "MIT OR Unlicense"
homepage = "https://github.com/AndrewAltimit/legend-of-legaia-re"
tags = ["endgame", "bosses", "quests", "minigames", "trading-cards"]
description = """
An expansion for the port that gives levelling to 99 a purpose: an \
endgame tower of new fights and superbosses tuned for a late-game party, \
a quest chain that threads them through the existing world, custom maps \
built from the disc's own scenery, trading cards collected as battle \
rewards and traded or sold, and new modes the original never had. It \
needs your own Legend of Legaia (NA) disc; the pack carries no game data.\
"""
schema = 3
disc = "SCUS-94254"
# Shown by the play page's pack library, the launcher and the workbench.
cover = "assets/cover.png"
# The oldest engine the pack is tested against.
min_engine = "0.1.0"

# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - progression.
#
# Retail's curve to level 99 asks for 9.6 million XP, 7.5 million of it
# past level 60, and the retail game has nothing left to fight by then.
# Rebirth keeps the retail steps through level 39 (the story), then cuts
# each step so a level costs between about 36,000 and 90,000 XP all the way
# up: 60 to 99 is about 2.5 million. With half again on every fight's EXP
# that is three to five field fights a level on the floor that matches it,
# and one or two for a gauntlet or a keeper. The README works the numbers
# through, and `crates/engine-expansion/tests/rebirth_balance.rs` checks
# them on the battle kernels.
# Format: docs/formats/expansion-pack-battle.md.

xp_mul = 1.5
gold_mul = 1.25

[xp_curve]
kind = "banded"
bands = [
    { from_level = 40, mul = 0.75 },
    { from_level = 45, mul = 0.62 },
    { from_level = 50, mul = 0.5 },
    { from_level = 55, mul = 0.43 },
    { from_level = 60, mul = 0.4 },
    { from_level = 65, mul = 0.37 },
    { from_level = 70, mul = 0.35 },
    { from_level = 80, mul = 0.33 },
    { from_level = 90, mul = 0.3 },
]

# The tower grows with the party, but slower than the party does: +0.5% to
# its monsters' stats and spoils per level of the strongest member past 50,
# at most x1.25 (level 100 would reach it). A level-99 party's ATK is half
# again its level-50 figure, so every level gained still counts, and a
# cleared floor stays worth a visit. Retail fights are left alone.
[enemy_scaling]
from_level = 50
per_level = 0.005
max_mul = 1.25
scope = "pack"
rewards = true

# Level 55, 80 and 99 are the climb's milestones: 55 is when the tower's
# first arts come (arts.toml), 80 the Knell finishers, 99 the Warden's
# last request and the First Breath (quests.toml).
[[level_rewards]]
level = 55
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 131 } }, { item = { kind = "item", id = 132 } }]

[[level_rewards]]
level = 60
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 121 }, count = 3 }]

[[level_rewards]]
level = 70
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 248 } }]

[[level_rewards]]
level = 80
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 249 } }]

[[level_rewards]]
level = 90
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 250 } }]

[[level_rewards]]
level = 99
items = [{ item = { kind = "item", id = 237 } }]

# Legend of Legaia: Rebirth - quests and challenges.
#
# The main chain climbs Genesis Tower floor by floor; side quests
# hang off the floors' NPCs. Dialogue is kept for what the player asks for
# and for story beats: a quest that starts or completes on its own (an
# auto-started quest, a count or a floor reached in the field) says nothing,
# and its quest toast and Journal entry carry it. A side quest an NPC hands
# out starts on its toast too, so one talk is never a queue of boxes. Every
# NPC here is a talk zone on a pack map
# (`[[triggers]] event = { kind = "talk", npc = ... }`), so "talking to"
# the Warden's Stone or the 2F brazier is stepping up to it. Pack flags
# and counters are the pack's own and never touch a retail story flag.
# Format: docs/formats/expansion-pack-quests.md.
#
# NPC ids and where they stand:
#   tower_guide    1F  the Warden's Stone, at the foot of the dais
#   ember_brazier  2F  the brazier between the middle pillars
#   vault_heart    4F  the sunken court
#   rest_keeper    5F  the keeper's counter
#   regent_seat    6F  the upper alcove
#   sanctum_echo   7F  the inner hall
#   hollow_throne  8F  the throne
